issues.legal_issue: The meaning given to a phrase in one statute does not determine its meaning in another statute when the statutes have different objects and definitions.
material_facts: The land was in an area governed by an earlier private-forest preservation law and was forest land under that law when the later vesting law took effect.
The landholder relied on a similar phrase in a separate land-reform statute to argue that its plantation was excluded from the definition of private forest.
issues.conclusion: The meaning of the phrase in the land-reform statute could not be transplanted into the vesting statute because the statutes had different objects and materially different definitions.
issues.legal_principle: Judicial interpretation of words in one statute does not guide their construction in another unless the statutes are pari materia. The court considered the different objects and definitions of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 and the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, including the latter's reference to the Madras Preservation of Private Forests Act, 1949. It referred to State of Kerala v. Anglo American D.T.T. Co. and State of Kerala v. K.C. Moosa Haji on the preservation law's treatment of land that was forest when that law applied, and distinguished Malankara Rubber and Produce Co. v. State of Kerala because that case did not concern land covered by the preservation law.

predicates.forest_vesting_proceeding: A proceeding concerns whether land is private forest subject to vesting in the government.
predicates.parallel_statutory_phrase_invoked: A landholder relies on the interpretation of a similar phrase in a separate statute to claim that land is excluded from the private-forest definition.
predicates.statutes_have_different_objects_or_defin: The statutes use materially different definitions or pursue different legislative objects.
predicates.land_was_forest_under_earlier_preservati: The land was treated as forest under an earlier preservation law applicable to it.

issues.definition: When a forest-vesting proceeding involves a similar phrase in statutes with different objects or definitions and land covered by an earlier preservation law, the phrase's meaning from the separate statute is not imported.

issues.legal_issue: The exclusion for land principally cultivated with an agricultural crop does not include plantations of non-fruit-bearing trees.
material_facts: The landholder maintained a large eucalyptus plantation for use as raw material in its manufacturing operation.
The land was forest under the earlier preservation law and remained so when the vesting law came into force.
The vesting law separately referred to fruit-bearing trees and to other agricultural crops, while its personal-cultivation exception addressed trees or plants of any species.
issues.conclusion: The phrase concerning other agricultural crops excludes only fruit-bearing trees, not eucalyptus plantations; the plantation land therefore remained within the private-forest definition and vested in the government.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(f)(1)(i)(C), 3(1), and 3(2) of the Kerala Private Forests (Vesting and Assignment) Act, 1971, the reference to other agricultural crops does not encompass all species of trees. The separate reference to cashew and other fruit-bearing trees, contrasted with the provision concerning cultivation of trees or plants of any species for the personal-cultivation exception, supports that construction. Agriculture can have a broad meaning that includes cultivated products of land, but it requires cultivation and does not include spontaneous forest growth. The court approved State of Kerala v. Amalgamated Malabar Estates, State of Kerala v. Malayalam Plantation Ltd., and State of Kerala v. K.C. Moosa Haji on the meaning of the exclusion, and referred to Commissioner of Income Tax v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy on agriculture and agricultural operations.

issues.definition: When a forest-vesting proceeding concerns land that remained forest under an earlier preservation law and the landholder cultivated non-fruit-bearing trees there, the land vests in the government.
